headline: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 19 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: Back to the mountains! After a couple of sprint stages and the ITT to kick-start the final week of La Vuelta 26, the riders face two mountain showdowns before Sunday’s finale in Granada. Today, they are in the province of Malaga, on familiar and demanding roads leading to a brutal summit finish at Peñas Blancas. The neutral start is set at 11:50, the start proper at 12:06 after an 8.3 km parade, and the winners should be crowned at around 17:30.

headline: The longest stage of La Vuelta 26
subtext: With 210.8 kilometres from Vélez-Málaga to Peñas Blancas, today is the longest stage of La Vuelta 26. The other 200+ kilometres stage of this edition was on day 2 (Monaco > Manosque, 202.1 km). But it was a rolling day, while today is a proper mountain stage, with over 4,000 metres of elevation gain. Will it also make for the longest day on the saddle? So far, the record was set at Alto de Aitana, when Enric Mas won stage 9 after 5 hours, 10 minutes and 40 seconds of racing.

headline: Welcome to Malaga
subtext: After Almeria, Granada, Jaen, Cordoba, Huelva, Seville, and Cadiz, La Vuelta 26 completes its Andalusian tour with a stage entirely set in the province of Malaga, the autonomous community’s eighth province. The race will then return to Granada for the final two stages of La Vuelta 26. Vélez-Málaga is a stage town for the second time in La Vuelta history, having hosted the start of stage 4 in 2018. It was the first mountain stage, to Alfacar, where Ben King took the win from the breakaway.

headline: Luis Angel Maté, the local icon
subtext: When stage 4 of La Vuelta 2018 set off from Vélez-Málaga, Luis Angel Maté also made the breakaway, defending his polka dot jersey and finishing 4th of the stage. Known as “El lince de Marbella” (Marbella’s lynx), he is an iconic cycling figure from the province of Malaga with 12 La Vuelta participations until he retired after the 2024 edition. This morning, Luis Angel Maté rode his bike en route to the final climb, where he plans to attend the stage on the roadside with his family and his friends.

headline: 10 years ago…
subtext: On 11 September 2016, Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility) won in Madrid the final stage of La Vuelta 16, three days after opening his Grand Tour tally in Gandia (stage 18). At the time, he was 23 and claimed his first successes away from Scandinavia. Now aged 33, he has 36 professional wins under his belt, including stages in the three Grand Tours (6 at La Vuelta, 2 in the Tour, 1 in the Giro), and is about to retire.

headline: Let’s roll
subtext: The peloton make their way to the start proper with an 8.3 km parade.

headline: La Roja
subtext: Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) was the best of the GC contenders in the ITT, but Enric Mas (Movistar) surpassed the expectations as he only lost 33 seconds to the Slovenian. Roglic is back in second place, 1’37’’ behind the Spaniard. Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) fell down to third place, with a gap 3’01’’. The trio are set to battle for the podium while Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) trails by 5’17’’ and Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) by 6’03’’.

headline: Green jersey
subtext: With another top 5 result, Wout van Aert put himself out of reach from any rival except his Visma-Lease a Bike teammate Matthew Brennan. The Belgian has 306 points, the Briton has 239 (-77). Alessandro Romele (XDS Astana) is third, 135 points behind Van Aert. A rider can grab a maximum of 130 points in the final three stages, including 40 today (20 at the finish, 20 at the intermediate sprint).

headline: Polka dot jersey
subtext: After three days with no categorised climbs, Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) still leads the mountains standings with 69 points, a tally that gives him a significant margin on Wout van Aert (40 points). Enric Mas (Movistar) follows with 24 points. There are 53 points up for grabs this week, and they’re all packed in stages 19 (20 points) and 20 (33 points).

headline: White jersey
subtext: Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) was happy with his TT performance yesterday. Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious) now trails by 57’’, and Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) is 12’33’’ behind.

headline: Team standings
subtext: With Callum Thornley, Primoz Roglic and Finn Ficher-Black, Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe had the strongest collective performance yesterday. Decathlon CMA CGM still lead the overall team standings with a gap of 56’34’’ to XDS Astana and 1h13’46’’ to EF Education-EasyPost.

headline: Roads that witnessed La Vuelta history
subtext: The area has often been visited by La Vuelta, as illustrated by some of the stages passed on today’s route: - Rincon de la Victoria (km 13) saw Michael Storer win 10 in 2021, with Mauri Vansevenant in second place - Coin (km 61) hosted the start of stage 13 in 2017: MatteoTrentin won in Tomares with Gianni Moscon in second place - Yunquera (km 88.2) saw Ben O’Connor win stage 6 of La Vuelta 24 and take La Roja from Primoz Roglic - Ronda (km 122.6) saw John Degenkolb win stage 5 of La Vuelta 14 - Estepona (km 186.1) saw Dietrich Thurau claim the first leader’s jersey of the 1976 edition, before witnessing victories from José De Cauwer (1976) and Jaan Kirsipuu (1998). As for Malaga (km 27.4), it first appeared on the map of La Vuelta in 1936, the second edition of the race. Belgium’s Gustaf Deloor took his fifth stage win, the second that year, and went on to win La Vuelta for the second time in a row. More recently, Malaga hosted the Gran Salida of the 2018 edition. It was also the setting of the first stage in 2000 and 2006.

headline: Stage 19 is ON!
subtext: En route to the mountains of Malaga!

headline: First attacks
subtext: A group of six riders opened a small gap but the bunch is packed at km 2.

headline: Attacks keep flying
subtext: A lone rider opened a gap, five more attackers joined him, and no they're eight leaders at km 5!

headline: All together at km 7
subtext: There are numerous contenders for the breakaway, as described by Tobias Johannessen (Uno-X) at the start: "There has already been some talks in the peloton from some of the guys who want to go together. There’s a lot of teams that sees this as maybe the last opportunity for a big breakaway. I think all the teams will want to have one guy, so maybe we just have to count, and then when everyone has one guy we can go.”

headline: No risks, no glory?
subtext: The bunch is packed at km 10, just before Rincon de la Victoria, where Michael Storer won stage of La Vuelta 21. That day, Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora_hansgrohe) attacked, crashed, and famously said: “No risk, no glory”. Are the Slovenian star and his team ready to risk it all in the final stages of La Vuetla 26? “Today and tomorrow are two days where that quote is perfect to use", Callum Thornley said at the start. "We’ll see what happens out there on the road.”

headline: 2 riders on the move: Wilksch and Wenzel
subtext: Hannes Wilksch (Tudor) and Mats Wenzel (Kern Pharma) are 12 seconds ahead of the peloton at km 13. Rudy Porter (Jayco AlUla) is in between.

headline: 4 chasers
subtext: Ivo Oliveira (UAE Emirates XRG), Lennard Kämna (Lidl-Trek) and Timo De Jong (Picnic PostNL) are with Rudy Porter (Jayco AlUla).

headline: The attackers are caught at km 19
subtext: The route is absolutely flat until Malaga (km 27.4). Then, there will be some gentle hills before the proper ascents of the day.

headline: 8 riders on the move
subtext: They've set off at km 21.

headline: Back together at km 22
subtext: Breakaway artist and La Vuelta veteran Jesus Herrada (Burgos Burpellet BH) spoke about the race dynamics he expected for today's stage: "I reckon a very large breakaway of around 20–30 riders could form, just like on other days, with riders who aren’t too close in the general classification, and that breakaway could gain some time. And then, once we’re in there, we’ll see who the strongest ones are."

headline: Paul Double withdraws from La Vuelta 26
subtext: The British puncheur confessed last week he was struggling a lot and felt like "one of the worst riders inthe race at the moment". He tried to hang and was penultimate in the overall standings.

headline: More attacks...
subtext: But the bunch is packed at km 29.

headline: 3 attackers: Kruijswijk, Leknessund, Sütterlin
subtext: Steven Kruijswijk (Visma-Lease a Bike), Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) and Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla) are 15 seconds ahead of the peloton at km 34.

headline: The battle goes on
subtext: The three leaders are now riding 22 seconds ahead of the bunch, and there's one chaser in between.

headline: 40 kilometres of battle
subtext: The gap slightly increases: 28 seconds.

headline: Coquard in pursuit?
subtext: Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) attacked from the bunch but he's rapidly been reeled in.

headline: More riders want to make the break
subtext: But the bunch cover all the counter-attacks at the moment. Meanxhile, the leading trio push their advantage to 42''.

headline: Steven Krujswijk, Andreas Leknessund and Jasha Sütterlin
Leknessund, Kruijswijk and Sütterlin have already covered 50 km
subtext: +32'' Three chasers +40'' Peloton

headline: 2 chase groups
subtext: First, it's Bastien Tronchon (Groupama-FDJ United), Tobias Johannessen (Uno-X Mobility) and Fabian Weiss (Tudor). Ivo Oliveira (UAE Emirates XRG), Lennard Kämna (Lidl-Trek), Pau Marti (NSN) and Mats Wenzel (Kern Pharma) are a bit further behind. The peloton stril trail by 40 seconds.

headline: Oliveira joins the first chase group
subtext: Meanwhile, Kämna, Marti and Wenzel are caught by the bunch.

headline: 6 leaders after almost 60 kilometres
subtext: Ivo Oliveira (UAE Emirates XRG), Bastien Tronchon (Groupama-FDJ United) and Tobias Johannessen (Uno-X Mobility) join Steven Kruijswijk (Visma-Lease a Bike), Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) and Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla). The peloton trail by 27''. Fabian Weiss (Tudor) has been caught.

headline: Vermaerke in pursuit
subtext: At km 63, Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG) is 18'' behind the six leaders, while the peloton trail by 30 seconds.

headline: 7 leaders, including two UAE Emirates XRG riders
subtext: Ivo Oliveira dropped back momentarily to help Kevin Vermaerke close the gap.

headline: It's still a strong pace in the peloton
subtext: Soudal Quick-Step, EF Education-EasyPost and Visma-Lease a Bike are at the front, 40 seconds behind the leaders after 69 kilometres.

headline: Hayter accelerates; Paret-Peintre and Landa eye the breakaway
subtext: Valentin Paret-Peintre (Soudal Quick-Step) said at the start he and Mikel Landa are targetting the finish at Peñas Blancas: “I hope there’s still some fuel left in the tank. At least, that’s how it feels to me. We’ll see how it goes on the road, but I feel I’m still in pretty good shape. Today, tomorrow or even Sunday – there are three days left, three opportunities. I think today’s stage might be the one that suits me best on paper and the one most likely to see a breakaway, so perhaps that’s the best opportunity. There’s been a lot of talk about this finish, about this climb [with Mikel Landa]. He knows it well. He’s also got ambitions today, so we’ll see in the final stretch. If we’re both in the breakaway, we’ll be able to play our cards a bit better.”

headline: The battle continues on the first climb of the day
subtext: The seven leaders are 37'' away when they start the climb up Puerto de las Abejas (14.6 km at 4.3%). Attackers immediately set off from the peloton.

headline: EF Education-EasyPost to control the stage?
subtext: Richard Carapaz's teammates control every move on the climb. The seven leaders are only 35'' ahead.

headline: Sütterlin struggles to keep up at the front
subtext: Meanwhile, Iñigo Elosegui (Kern Pharma) and riders from XDS Astana increase the pace in the peloton. The gap is down to 15'' with 130 kilometres to go.

headline: Dunbar sets off from the bunch
subtext: Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5) rapidly closes the gap to the leaders. The peloton are right behind.

headline: Minimal gaps
subtext: With a flurry of attacks to shake the bunch, the leaders are only 5 seconds away. They have 7 kilometres to go to the summit.

headline: 5 kilometres to the summit
subtext: The six leaders keep pushing hard. Filippo Zana (Soudal Quick-Step), Darren van Bekkum (XDS Astana) and José Luis Faura (Burgos Burpellet BH) are 15 seconds behind. The gap to the bunch has slightly increased: 45 seconds.

headline: 9 leaders: Dunbar, Johannessen, Vermaerke, Zana...
subtext: Filippo Zana (Soudal Quick-Step), Darren van Bekkum (XDS Astana) and José Luis Faura (Burgos Burpellet BH) join Ivo Oliveira, Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5), Bastien Tronchon (Groupama-FDJ United), Tobias Johannessen, Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility) into the final 4 kilometres of the climb. More counter-attackers set off from the bunch.

headline: Onley and Carapaz on the move?
subtext: Into the final kilometre of ascent, Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) follows a move. Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) also reacts.

headline: And now 13 leaders: Nordhagen, Bisiaux, Dubar, Johannessen, Leknessund...
subtext: Jorgen Nordhagen (Visma-Lease a Bike), Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM), Rudy Molard (Groupama-FDJ United) and Ramses Debruyne (Alpecin-Premier Tech) join Ivo Oliveira, Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5), Bastien Tronchon (Groupama-FDJ United), Filippo Zana (Soudal Quick-Step), Tobias Johannessen, Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility), Darren van Bekkum (XDS Astana) and José Luis Faura (Burgos Burpellet BH) just before the summit. The last gap to the peloton: 28 seconds.

headline: The average speed after 2 hours: 46.1 km/h
subtext: And that includes the ascent up Puerto de las Abejas!

headline: Results at Puerto de las Abejas (cat. 2, km 91)
subtext: 1. Leknessund, 5 pts 2. Vermaerke, 3 pts 3. Faura, 1 pt

headline: More attacks on the second climb of the day
subtext: Pau Miquel (Bahrain Victorious), Valentin Madouas, Guillaume Martin-Guyonnet (Groupama-FDJ United), Sergio Samitier (Cofidis), Rudy Porter (Jayco AlUla), Jarno Widar (Lotto Intermarché) and Chris Hamilton (Picnic PostNL) are closing the gap to the 13 leaders up the Puerto del Viento (13.1km at 3.7%). The peloton are not far behind - Sepp Kuss (Visma-Lease a Bike) attacks.

headline: Sepp Kuss also joins the front group
subtext: As Sepp Kuss (Visma-Lease a Bike), Thomas Gloag (Pinarello Q36.5), Jan Hirt (NSN) and Harold Tejada (XDS Astana) join the front of the race, Netcompany Ineos pull the bunch a dozen of seconds behind.

headline: Dunbar leads the way, the attackers are caught
subtext: The Irishman is 10.5 km from the summit of the Puerto del Viento.

headline: A Pinarello Q36.5 duo to lead the way
subtext: Thomas Gloag is chasing 15 seconds behind Eddie Dunbar. More attackers set off from the bunch, 15 seconds further behind. Meanwhile, many riders are dropped, including Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike).

headline: The GC battle begins more than 100 kilometres from the finish
subtext: As a small group gets away, Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) gets on the move. Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) reacts, followed by Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), and then Enric Mas (Movistar).

headline: Dunbar still leads the way, a new group emerges
subtext: Eddie Dunbar (Pinarello Q36.5) will soon reach the summit and enter the final 100 kilometres of the stage. A group of chasers have set off with Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Thomas Gloag (Pinarello Q36.5), Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility)... More climbers attack from the bunch, including Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious).

headline: Dunbar leads the way to the summit
subtext: Not far behind, Buitrago is second with his polka dot jersey.

headline: Carapaz has attacked again!
subtext: The Ecuadorian icon is leading a small chase group over the top of the Puerto del Viento.

headline: 17 leaders: Dunbar, Buitrago, Leknessund...
subtext: UAE Emirates XRG: Vermaerke Movistar: Castrillo Pinarello Q36.5: Camprubi, Dunbar, Gloag Bahrain Victorious: Buitrago, Miquel Groupama-FDJ United: Martin-Guyonnet, Molard, Tronchon Uno-X Mobility: Leknessund Cofidis: Samitier EF Education-EasyPost: Rafferty XDS Astana: Van Bekkum Picnic PostNL: Hamilton Kern Pharma: Berrade, Wenzel

headline: The situation after 120 kilometres
subtext: The 17-man breakaway are on rolling terrain. +40'' Ivo Oliveira (UAE Emirates XRG), Jan Hirt (NSN), Filippo Zana (Soudal Quick-Step), Koen Bouwman (Jayco AlUla), Larry Warbasse (Tudor), Gijs Leemreize (Picnic PostNL) Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) drives another chase group also featuring Marco Brenner (Tudor), Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM), Jorgen Nordhagen (Visma-Lease a Bike)... +1'25'' Peloton

headline: Rafferty suffers a mechanical while pulling for Carapaz
subtext: Richard Carapaz and his chase companions are 1'05'' behind the leaders and 20'' ahead of the bunch with 86 kilometres to go.

headline: The chasers: Carapaz, Brenner, Bisiaux...
subtext: Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe: Tuckwell UAE Emirates XRG: Oliveira Visma-Lease a Bike: Nordhagen Decathlon CMA CGM: Bisiaux Pinarello Q36.5: Vader NSN: Hirt Soudal Quick-Step: Zana Jayco AlUla: Bouwman EF Education-EasyPost: Carapaz Tudor: Brenner, Warbasse Lotto Intermarché: Widar Picnic PostNL: Leemreize

headline: Carapaz sits back and waits for the bunch
subtext: Among the chasers, Gijs Leemreize (Picnic PostNL) continues his effort to try and join the leaders.

headline: The situation after 130 kilometres of battle
subtext: There are 16 riders at the front (among the 17 riders previously announced, Rafferty dropped back). +1'05'' Leemreize +1'25'' Romeo paces the bunch

headline: The situation settles after a brutal first 3 hours
subtext: Gijs Leemreize (Picnic PostNL) has been cuaght by the bunch, now trailing by 2 minutes.
